title: IBM ReRAM pulse-count program-and-verify endpoint model
hypothesis: An adaptive fixed-amplitude pulse-count controller reduces verify reads relative to one-pulse verify without materially increasing held-out endpoint error or failure probability, and a target-dependent Gaussian is adequate only when its predeclared coverage and Wasserstein gates pass.
motivation: Establish the programming boundary needed to compare HWA-only deployment with later matched Tiki-Taka or LoRA recovery, without assuming that on-chip training is required.

arms.description: Optimized-material IBM array fit with corruption disabled for continuous endpoint modeling.
Optimized-material population with the published corrupt-device probability enabled.
Baseline-HfO2 stress control with corruption disabled.
Baseline-HfO2 population with the published corrupt-device probability enabled.

completion_criteria: All four declared arms complete the 41-target, three-tolerance, two-start, two-controller design on 4096 device identities with eight repeats.
Trajectory and verify-event artifacts preserve accepted, failed, saturated, non-finite, and corrupt outcomes with exact seeds and sampled device state.
Gaussian adequacy is decided only by the predeclared coverage and normalized Wasserstein gates on held-out device identities.
Wan-2022 raw and explicitly clipped one-second comparisons are present with the normalization and timing limitations stated.
No HWA, Tiki-Taka, LoRA, or network-accuracy conclusion is drawn from this device-characterization study.
analysis_plan: Compare adaptive and one-pulse controllers within each matched preset, start protocol, target, and tolerance using success, endpoint residual, pulses, verifies, and reversals.
Fit fourth-order target-dependent mean and log-standard-deviation models on fit identities and validate coverage and target-binned Wasserstein distance on held-out validation identities.
Keep corrupt and failed trajectories in separate target-conditioned failure models rather than absorbing them into continuous Gaussian variance.
Compare IBM apparent endpoints with Wan-2022 at one second in the common normalized coordinate, reporting both native raw and explicit [0,1]-clipped Wan views.
